handoff_meta.title: 40k Reforged Listbuilder Project - AI Handoff
handoff_meta.project: Warhammer 40k Reforged Homebrew listbuilder / New Recruit catalogue project
handoff_meta.purpose: This document transfers the current state of the project from one AI/chat to the next. It is intentionally exhaustive about recent work, current files, unresolved questions, dependencies, and pickup context.
handoff_meta.critical_length_instruction: THERE IS NO MAXIMUM LENGTH OR SIZE FOR A PROJECT HANDOFF. Continuity is more important than brevity.
handoff_meta.staleness_contract: THIS HANDOFF IS INTENTIONALLY A POINT-IN-TIME SNAPSHOT AND IS EXPECTED TO BECOME STALE AS WORK CONTINUES. Use it to understand recent project state and reasoning, not as permanent authoring doctrine. Current executable files, authoritative source rules, the current Game System, the current Maintenance Guide, and observed New Recruit runtime behavior outrank stale statements in this handoff.
handoff_meta.why_v2_exists: The original handoff successfully onboarded multiple chats because it preserved enormous amounts of context. Over time it also accumulated permanent doctrine and temporary project state in the same artifact. V2 preserves the exhaustive continuity function while moving durable doctrine to the Game System and repeatable procedure to the Maintenance Guide.

read_order: Read this handoff completely enough to understand current state and unresolved work.
Research current New Recruit / BattleScribe documentation before relying on remembered schema behavior.
Read the current Game System and Catalogue Maintenance & Presentation Guide.
Inspect the current executable catalogue/library files relevant to the task.
authority_boundary: This handoff owns continuity, not permanent doctrine.
The authoritative army rules PDF / UUS owns faction game meaning.
The current Game System owns reusable cross-faction listbuilder doctrine and proven engine conventions.
The current executable catalogue and linked libraries own deployed implementation state.
Observed New Recruit runtime behavior owns engine reality.
The Catalogue Maintenance & Presentation Guide owns recurring maintenance/update procedure.
Historical handoffs and archived documents are archaeology once superseded.
how_to_use_this_handoff.conflict_rule: If this handoff disagrees with a current file or current canonical document, do not preserve the handoff blindly. Identify the disagreement, determine whether the handoff is stale, and use the current source appropriate to that kind of truth.
how_to_use_this_handoff.promotion_rule: If current work establishes a reusable cross-faction lesson, promote the durable lesson into the Game System. If it establishes repeatable maintenance procedure, promote it into the Maintenance Guide. Do not rely on future handoffs to preserve permanent doctrine.

cadence: Implementation-first for clearly understood fixes and established patterns.
Discuss genuinely weird/nontrivial mechanics before implementation.
User manually tests generated JSON in New Recruit and reports observed behavior.
Observed New Recruit behavior and screenshots are ground truth for engine behavior.
Current executable files override stale comments and old handoffs.
maintenance_boundary: A catalogue-maintenance request normally begins with an audit unless the user explicitly asks to implement immediately.
Straightforward established presentation cleanup can be applied directly when requested.
Do not broaden a targeted task into a rules redesign.
Bugfix bullets are only for states that actually went live.
Source-derived rules descriptions remain verbatim unless the authoritative source changes.
artifact_expectation: Use deterministic IDs only for genuinely new objects.
When portable shared content changes intrinsically, synchronize the owned library/source in the same pass.

important_current_project_truths: The listbuilder is a companion to the army rules PDF and a fancy notepad, not a replacement rules engine.
The builder represents meaningful final player decisions rather than blindly replaying procedural replacement wording.
Source game meaning belongs to the authoritative army rules / UUS. New Recruit is an output format.
Current executable data and observed New Recruit runtime behavior outrank stale comments or historical handoffs.
Presentation categories are not semantic authority.
The Game System now explicitly separates player-facing UI shape from semantic validation.
A stock New Recruit constraint may be relaxed or removed when the same legality is preserved through a cleaner constructive validator.
Selected-hidden states are invalid and should be avoided.
Optional model and direct max-1 upgrade checkbox behavior have been runtime-proven and are documented in the current Game System.
Comments should describe current state and intentional rationale, not accumulate archaeology indefinitely.
Shared libraries own intrinsic reusable unit-tree content; consumer catalogues own host-specific availability, presentation, and consumer-local semantics.

known_superseded_legacy_guidance.why_it_matters: The old August handoff hardcoded the older ID.

known_superseded_legacy_guidance.legacy: Additional Copy Costs apply only to Other units and Troops have no generic copy allowance.
known_superseded_legacy_guidance.current: Current Game System uses separate Troop and Other ledgers. Troops use 4 / 6 / 8 normal-copy allowances at 800 / 1200 / 1600; Other uses 1 / 2 / 3. Each excess identical copy costs +20 Points.
known_superseded_legacy_guidance.why_it_matters: Do not resurrect the August Other-only architecture.

known_superseded_legacy_guidance.legacy: Standard top-level labels include Additional Leader, Special Weapon Loadouts, and Additional Models.
known_superseded_legacy_guidance.current: Do not use Special Weapon Loadouts merely as taxonomy; use singular Additional Model for the max-one pattern; use meaningful Attached [MODEL / LEADER] relationship names instead of generic Additional Leader when player-facing.
known_superseded_legacy_guidance.why_it_matters: The presentation grammar matured during the catalogue sweep.

known_superseded_legacy_guidance.legacy: Single paid wargear should be wrapped in an optional max-1 subgroup to avoid a spinner.
known_superseded_legacy_guidance.current: Direct optional upgrade + max 1 is the proven checkbox-style pattern. Do not add a one-item wrapper merely to force presentation.
known_superseded_legacy_guidance.why_it_matters: The August Sororitas-era workaround was superseded by later runtime proof.

known_superseded_legacy_guidance.legacy: Maintain a large named library of standard error templates.
known_superseded_legacy_guidance.current: Game System REV23 retired the large template library. Prefer structural prevention when clean; otherwise use the three-part corrective pattern: invalid condition, allowed condition, repair.
known_superseded_legacy_guidance.why_it_matters: Do not rebuild the retired template bureaucracy.

known_superseded_legacy_guidance.legacy: Harlequins are the canonical current reference implementation and Drukhari is the immediate next task.
known_superseded_legacy_guidance.current: Harlequins remain useful historical/proven examples, but no faction is permanently privileged as the sole reference. Drukhari maintenance is complete through REV33.
known_superseded_legacy_guidance.why_it_matters: This was temporary August project state.

known_superseded_legacy_guidance.legacy: Cross-model ancestor hiding is broadly preferred for weapon caps.
known_superseded_legacy_guidance.current: Cross-hide is an engine capability, not a default design goal. Prefer local clean prevention only when it cannot hide an already-selected choice; otherwise permissive-corrective validation is often safer.
known_superseded_legacy_guidance.why_it_matters: Selected-hidden invalid states and brittle dependencies are now explicitly avoided.

legacy_runtime_observations_not_to_lose.status: These observations came from the successful August handoff and later work. Many are already represented in the current Game System. If one is absent there, treat this handoff entry as continuity evidence, not automatic permanent doctrine; verify current runtime before promoting it.
observations: Nested units can be valid Association targets.
Shared-library sharedSelectionEntries with importRootEntries:false plus consumer-local entryLinks work.
Cross-library categories/associations have worked in deployed project structures.
Modifiers with repeats can implement dynamic copy-cost arithmetic.
Candidate-side association-count invalidation can self-invalidate after attachment and should not be used casually for host exclusivity.
A selected entry becoming hidden creates invalid state. Avoid selected-hidden designs.
Dynamically revealed mandatory/default child selectors may not instantiate their default exactly as expected and require runtime testing.
Root Configuration selections appear as siblings.
Multiple separate association pickers can permit duplicate targeting unless the structure prevents it.
Custom player-facing errors can be emitted with modifier field='error'.
Auto-granted nested units can remain fully configurable.
Association logic can discover nested units.

what_the_next_ai_should_do_on_pickup: Research current New Recruit / BattleScribe documentation rather than relying only on model memory.
Inspect the actual current catalogue/library files relevant to the user's next request.
If the request concerns an army-rules version update, use the Maintenance Guide V3 minimal update contract rather than asking the user to restate routine maintenance steps.

closing_context.project_state: The project is mature enough that documentation boundaries now matter as much as individual catalogue mechanics. The successful cold-start process is being preserved while the authority surfaces are being separated cleanly.
closing_context.central_continuity_rule: Preserve context generously, but preserve permanent knowledge in its permanent home.
closing_context.length_restatement: THERE IS NO MAXIMUM LENGTH OR SIZE FOR A PROJECT HANDOFF. A future AI should receive enough current context to continue safely without archaeological guesswork.
